goals: Explain why we hold out test data
Split data correctly, including stratified and time-based splits
Use a validation set for tuning
why: A model scored on the data it learned from always looks better than it really is. The test set is your only honest preview of real-world performance.
explain: If students are graded on the exact questions they practised, a high score proves memory, not understanding. Models are the same.
Split once at the start: typically 70–80% **train**, 20–30% **test**. Lock the test set away and use it **once**, at the very end.
To tune settings (hyperparameters), carve a **validation** set out of the training data, or better, use cross-validation. Tuning on the test set quietly turns it into training data.

**Stratify** classification splits so that class proportions match (important when only 2% of rows are fraud). For time series, split **by time**: train on the past, test on the future. Never shuffle time.

example.title: Stratifying a fraud dataset
steps: 10,000 card transactions, 200 frauds (2%); 80/20 split → train 8,000 rows, test 2,000 rows
Perfectly proportional: 2% of 2,000 = 40 frauds in test, 160 in train
A purely random split averages 40 test frauds but with SD ≈ 5.6: about a 9% chance of 30 or fewer, or 50 or more
With, say, 28 test frauds, each missed fraud moves recall by more than 3.5 points
stratify=y forces exactly 40 frauds into test and 160 into train
example.result: Both sets carry the true 2% fraud rate, so the test score is not distorted by an unlucky shuffle.

mistakes: Peeking at the test score repeatedly while tuning.
takeaways: Train on one part, judge on another
Stratify for imbalanced classes; split by time for time series

practice.code:
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
import numpy as np
y = np.array([0] * 9800 + [1] * 200); X = np.arange(len(y)).reshape(-1, 1)
X_tr, X_te, y_tr, y_te = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2, stratify=y, random_state=42)
print(y_te.mean(), y_tr.mean())     # both 0.02

check.q: You tuned 50 models and picked the best test score. The problem?
options: The test set has been used for selection, so the score is optimistic
check.why: Choosing on the test set leaks it into model selection. Use validation or cross-validation.

check.q: Correct split for monthly sales forecasting?
options: Train on earlier months, test on later months
check.why: The future must never inform the past.
